correctness.rationale: For every \(d\ge6\), an explicit \(2d\)-center covering supplies scale \(r=(d-1)/d\) for all real x, including equality boundaries. At \(\lambda<r\), each of \(2d\) vertices forces one distinct cover; all \(2^d\) facet barycenters lie at L1-distance \(\ge2r\) from vertices and hence need \(\le3\) other covers. Adjacent facet barycenters with sign Hamming distance \(\ge d-1\) are mutually \(>2\lambda\) apart, producing a forbidden three-coloring. Theorem 3.3 of Harney–Gluesing-Luerssen establishes \(\chi(H_2(d,d-1))=4\) for all \(d\ge3\), exactly the defined adjacency. Finite checker independently reproduces distance equalities, sign coloring, and rational-grid coverage, without conflating finite tests and infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Joós (arXiv:2305.00569, Conjecture 2) explicitly asks for exactly this equality in \(d\ge6\), not established by the paper’s results in \(d=4,5\). Harney and Gluesing-Luerssen (Theorem 3.3) establish \(\chi(H_2(d,d-1))=4\) but do not claim a crosspolytope homothetic-covering consequence. The present argument newly identifies the facet-barycenter incompatibility graph and converts a hypothetical cover into a three-coloring. Indexed semantic searches, own-claim comparisons and related full-text inspections did not reveal a theorem implying the asserted \(d\ge6\) value. Unindexed or inaccessible prior coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: The recent 2026 full text was inaccessible, although its abstract treats the different \(2^d\)-copy upper-bound functional.
Unindexed papers, independent unpublished proofs or indirect stronger theorems might exist; indexed absence is not proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The result resolves Joós’s explicit Conjecture 2 for every remaining dimension \(d\ge6\). This is a natural sharp homothetic self-covering invariant of a central convex body, not an artificial parametric slice or a tiny unmotivated improvement. The crosspolytope-to-Hamming graph reduction replaces known low-dimensional casework by a uniform obstruction; the exact numerical value is the point of the source conjecture.
